sections.label: Editions
sections.description: Fedora Editions are the official OS editions of Fedora Linux.

links.label: Workstation
links.description: The flagship Fedora edition featuring the latest Gnome desktop. The Linux desktop you've been waiting for.

links.label: Server
links.description: Run applications on bare metal or the cloud with a Linux server OS packed with the latest open source technology.

links.label: IoT
links.description: A foundation for Internet of Things and Device Edge ecosystem.

links.label: CoreOS
links.description: An automatically-updating, minimal operating system for running containerized workloads securely and at scale.

links.label: Cloud
links.description: An automatically-updating, minimal operating system for running containerized workloads securely and at scale.

sections.label: Emerging Editions
sections.description: These editions are supported but not yet a part of the official Fedora editions.

links.label: Silverblue
links.description: Fedora Silverblue is an immutable desktop operating system aimed at good support for container-focused workflows.

sections.label: Spins
sections.description: The Desktop spins feature specific Linux Desktop Environments. Our official Workstation Edition uses the Gnome Desktop, but you can install Fedora preconfigured with any of the listed Desktop Environments.

links.label: Fedora KDE
links.description: A complete, modern desktop built using the KDE Plasma Desktop Environment.

links.label: Fedora XFCE
links.description: A complete and well integrated desktop.

links.label: Cinnamon Desktop
links.description: A modern desktop featuring a traditional gnome user experience.

links.label: Mate-Compiz Desktop
links.description: A classic Fedora desktop with an additional 3D window manager.

links.label: i3 Tiling WM
links.description: Fedora Linux with the i3 Tiling Window Manager.

links.label: LXQT Desktop
links.description: A lightweight and well intgrated LXQT desktop environment.

links.label: LXDE Desktop
links.description: A light, fast, and less resource hungry desktop environment

links.label: Kinoite
links.description: Fedora Kinoite is an immutable KDE-based desktop.

sections.label: Labs
sections.description: The Labs are Fedora Linux set up with software bundles based on particular topics.

links.label: Astronomy
links.description: Powerful, completely open-source and free tools for amateur and professional astronomers.

links.label: Comp Neuro
links.description: A plethora of Free/Open source computational modelling tools for Neuroscience.

links.label: Design Suite
links.description: Visual design, multimedia production, and publishing suite of free and open source creative tools.

links.label: Games
links.description: A collection and perfect showcase of the best games available in Fedora.

links.label: Jam
links.description: For audio enthusiasts and musicians who want to create, edit, and produce audio and music on Linux.

links.label: Python Classroom
links.description: A classroom lab for teaching the Python programming language to students.

links.label: Robotics Suite
links.description: A wide variety of free and open robotics software packages for beginners and experts.

links.label: Scientific
links.description: A bundle of open source scientific and numerical tools used in research.

links.label: Security Lab
links.description: A bundle of open source scientific and numerical tools used in research.

contributors.label: Contributors
contributors.description: These pages connect you to all the different spaces that Fedorans work on projects. From new to long-term contributors, the following links will get you to where you want to go.

sections.label: Accounts & Apps
sections.description: These are some of the tools that you will use when contributing to the Fedora Project.

links.label: Fedora Accounts
links.description: To be granted access to things and to be credited for your contributions, you will need a Fedora account. Do this first!

links.label: Mote
links.description: Most subprojects hold weekly meetings in chatrooms. Fedora's Zodbot listens in on these meetings and keeps the logs here. The logs are open for everyone to browse.

links.label: Badges
links.description: This is where contributors are awarded tokens of recognition for their contributions. How many can you get!

links.label: Elections
links.description: To expedite the decission making process, talented leaders are elected to oversee the Fedora Project and Fedora's subprojects.

links.label: Fedocal
links.description: It's Fedora's calendar!

links.label: Mailing Lists
links.description: Yes, they still exist.

links.label: Edit this website
links.description: Edit fedoraproject.org pages using its custom content management system! Tip: Use the GitLab SSO link to open a session first.

sections.label: Packaging & Development
sections.description: These are the tools and Git forges that Fedora packagers and developers use to build the Fedora systems.

links.label: Bugzilla
links.description: Fedora bugs are reported to Red Hat's bugzilla.

links.label: Bodhi
links.description: This is Fedora's official build system. It is used to create, test, and publish packages.

links.label: Koji
links.description: This is the software that builds Fedora's RPM packages.

links.label: Copr
links.description: This is an easy-to-use build system for the Fedora community.

links.label: GitLab
links.description: GitLab is the newest of Fedora's official version control systems. It supports single-sign-on with Fedora accounts.

links.label: GitHub
links.description: Many of Fedora's groups use this version control system.

links.label: Pagure
links.description: This is an open-source git forge that the Fedora Project uses.

links.label: Package Sources
links.description: This is an open-source git forge that hosts most of Fedora's source RPM packages.

sections.label: Documentation
sections.description: These documentation pages are contributor-focused. They include Fedora's guidelines, teams, organizational structure, and legal docs.

links.label: Edit these docs
links.description: Did you notice a glaring typo or a broken link in these docs? Click here to find out how you can help make it right!

sections.label: New Contributors
sections.description: We are always excited to work with new contributors. If you're new to the project, check out these sites.

links.label: Join SIG
links.description: This is a special interest group that has formed for the sole purpose of helping new contributors get involved. Fedora is big and complex and it needs your help!

links.label: Easy Fix
links.description: These are some low-priority items that are thought to be good entry-level tasks for a new contributor to start with.

connections.label: Connections
connections.description: These are places to get (and give) user support.

sections.label: News & Publications
sections.description: These are sites where updates about new and upcomming events, releases, packages, and projects are likely to be posted. You might want to subscribe to some of these to get the notices in your inbox.

links.label: News & Announcements
links.description: The Fedora Project Leader likes to post things here. This forum also receives weekly updates from The Fedora Project Manager and the Community Platform Engineering team.

links.label: Fedora Magazine
links.description: Fedora new release and beta release announcements show up here first. Test Day announcements are also posted here. This blog also hosts articles contributed from users like you!

links.label: Fedora Community Blog
links.description: Announcements that are pertinent to Fedora developers and the Fedora infrastructure team tend to be posted here.

links.label: Fedora Mastodon
links.description: Follow us on Mastodon! This is a great place to stay up to date on the latest in the Fedora community.

links.label: Fedora Twitter
links.description: Follow us on twitter! This is a great place to stay up to date on the latest in the Fedora community.

sections.label: Ask Fedora
sections.description: This is Fedora's main forum for all project collaboration and user support.

links.label: General Q&A
links.description: If you need help installing, using, or customizing Fedora Linux, or have any other questions about the operating system or the Fedora Project, this is the place to ask!

links.label: Workstation
links.description: Use this link to focus on questions and answers about Fedora Workstation.

links.label: Server
links.description: Use this link to focus on questions and answers about Fedora Server.

links.label: Cloud
links.description: Use this link to focus on questions and answers about Fedora Cloud.

links.label: IoT
links.description: Use this link to focus on questions and answers about Fedora IoT (Internet of Things).

links.label: CoreOS
links.description: Use this link to focus on questions and answers about Fedora CoreOS.

sections.label: Project Discussion
sections.description: These are some convenient links to the discussion threads for several of Fedora's larger subprojects.

sections.label: Social & Events
sections.description: These are a few free-form communication channels and some links to information about Fedora's release parties and annual conferences. Fedorans regularly come together to celebrate our community and the hard work that we put into it!

links.label: The Water Cooler
links.description: This is the proverbial office “water cooler”, where people gather for “break from work” conversation. Introduce yourself, have (friendly!) off-topic discussions, and socialize!

links.label: Fedora Social
links.description: The Fedora Social chat room is a place for Fedora community members to relax and talk about most any topics they wish.

links.label: Extended Social Channels
links.description: Beyond the official channels for Fedorans to communicate, community members are involved on other popular platforms as well! Check out IRC, Discord, Telegram, Reddit, and more!

links.label: Week of Diversity
links.description: This is a week in September where we highlight the contributions and experiences of women, lgbtq+, and bipoc in Fedora.

links.label: Flock To Fedora
links.description: The annual contributor conference for Fedora Linux. Flock takes place at the beginning of August.

links.label: Release Parties
links.description: Fedora releases two major versions every year. We celebrate the hard work of our contributors virtually at each release.

sections.label: User Guides
sections.description: These are some introductory guides to help users get started with Fedora Linux.

links.label: Downloading Fedora Linux
links.description: How to select the appropriate download.

links.label: Getting Started
links.description: An in-depth guide to installing Fedora Linux.

links.label: Upgrading Fedora Linux
links.description: How to upgrade an existing Fedora Linux installation.

sections.label: Other Sources
sections.description: Over the years, Fedorans have created many sources of information about Fedora Linux and the Fedora Project.

links.label: Fedora Docs
links.description: This is the main index page for all of Fedora's Documentation. If you weren't able to find a direct link to what you were looking for in this site's menus, you can try searching from here.

links.label: Fedora Quick Docs
links.description: This is a collection of short HOWTO and FAQ-style documentation for Fedora users.

links.label: Fedora Wiki
links.description: This is primarily a collaboration tool for the community. Content that has been submitted here might be out of date and/or it might not have undergone the same level of scrutiny as the information on Fedora Docs.

links.label: Fedora Developer
links.description: From mobile apps to web; from desktop to GUIs to CLI tools; create it all easily with Fedora.

sections.label: About
sections.description: The Fedora Project is a community of people working together to build a free and open source software platform and to collaborate on and share user-focused solutions built on that platform. Or, in plain English, we make an operating system and we make it easy for you to do useful stuff with it.
